text:
Bitcoin held a $64,000–$64,500 range the evening of June 22, displaying relative strength against an altcoin drawdown. Sentiment is stabilizing as the aggressive institutional exodus from spot Bitcoin ETFs decelerates. Concurrently, infrastructure is maturing, highlighted by ICE and OKX launching a joint venture to build a U.S.-regulated broker-dealer, and Franklin Templeton solidifying its "Franklin Crypto" division.

Simultaneously, regulatory perimeters are hardening. The EU rapidly approaches its July 1 MiCA transition cliff, while U.S. federal agencies advance proposals classifying stablecoin issuers as financial institutions to enforce rigorous AML standards.

This structural maturation must contend with a restrictive macroeconomic reality. With the 2-year Treasury yield at a 16-month high of 4.23%, the 10-year yield anchoring at 4.50%, and the DXY commanding 101.0, risk-free rates exert immense gravity. Until Thursday's crucial PCE inflation print provides disinflationary relief, crypto multiples will remain compressed relative to record-high traditional equities.
